scenes.say: Happy New Year! Here is one resolution your eyes will love. Move more.

scenes.en: The retina and optic nerve need steady blood supply.
scenes.say: Number three. Better blood flow. The retina and the optic nerve need a steady supply of blood and oxygen, and regular exercise supports healthy circulation.

scenes.en: Exercise helps control diabetes and BP, which protect the eyes.
scenes.say: Number two. Exercise helps keep blood sugar and blood pressure in control. Both, when high, can damage the tiny blood vessels in your eyes.

scenes.en: Outdoor play in daylight helps lower the risk of short sight.
scenes.say: Number one. For children, playing outdoors in daylight is linked to a lower risk of short sight. So walk together as a family.

scenes.en: Studies suggest active people have a lower risk of some eye diseases.
scenes.say: Did you know? Studies suggest people who stay active have a lower risk of some eye diseases, like glaucoma.

scenes.en: 30 minutes a day. Sunglasses in strong sun. Never look at the sun.
scenes.say: Start small. Thirty minutes of brisk walking a day. Wear sunglasses in strong sun, and never look straight at the sun.

scenes.en: Start the year with a family eye test.
scenes.say: Start the new year right. Book an eye test for your family.
